name: seomatic-weekly-brief
description: >-
  Use when the user asks for a weekly SEO brief, a weekly SEO update, or what
  changed this week, from real Search Console data via SEOmatic.
---
# Weekly SEO brief

Every read below is Search Console or site data: free, and uses none of SEOmatic's free monthly questions.

1. **Compare the weeks**: `gsc_performance` for the last 7 days against the 7 before (clicks, impressions, the pages and queries that moved most). Use site totals, not a sum of the top rows: a top-N cut invents losses.
2. **Explain any drop before calling it one**: a query that lost clicks at the same position is usually a SERP feature or seasonality, not a ranking loss. `gsc_insights` separates the two. Never claim which SERP feature took the clicks unless a tool shows it.
3. **Pick ONE action**, backed by a number from the data (a striking-distance query with its impressions, or a page whose click-through is far below its position's norm).
4. **Write it in under 150 words**: what changed, why, the one thing to do. If nothing meaningful changed, say so in one line; don't pad.
5. If Search Console is not connected, say so and relay the connect link the tool returns. `get_started` gives a site check without it.

skills.name: seomatic-traffic-drop
skills.description: Use when the user says traffic, clicks or rankings fell, or asks what happened to their SEO: diagnoses the drop from real Search Console data via SEOmatic and ranks what to fix.
skills.content:
---
name: seomatic-traffic-drop
description: >-
  Use when the user says traffic, clicks or rankings fell, or asks what happened
  to their SEO: diagnoses the drop from real Search Console data via SEOmatic
  and ranks what to fix.
---
# Traffic drop diagnosis

Never ask for a domain. If GSC isn't connected, send https://app.seomatic.ai/connect/gsc and stop.

## 1. Confirm the drop is real
`gsc_insights` action `seasonality` first (16 months YoY). A seasonal dip isn't a problem; say so. Then `gsc_performance` action `compare_periods` (28d vs prior 28d) and action `trend` to find the start day. A one-day cliff points to a change; a slow slope to competition or decay. GSC lags 2-3 days; for the last 48h use action `fresh` and say numbers are provisional.

## 2. Find where the clicks went
- `gsc_performance` action `folder_rollup`: sitewide or one section?
- `compare_periods` on pages, then queries: 10 biggest losers with position before/after.
- Position steady but clicks down: demand fell or a SERP feature took the click; check `serp_competitors` action `features`.
- Position down: outranked or the page changed.

## 3. Rule out technical causes
`gsc_indexing` action `batch_inspect` on top losing URLs. `gsc_insights` action `sitemaps`. `site_pages` action `crawl` on the two biggest losers to see if title/H1/body changed.

## 4. Rule out measurement
If GA4 is connected, `traffic_analytics` action `sources` for the same window.

## 5. Verdict, then fixes
One sentence: cause, confidence, evidence. Then fixes ranked by clicks recovered. Say what you couldn't check.

## Staging (paid plan only)
Check `task_manage` action `list` to avoid duplicates, then `create` up to 5 tasks: `content_refresh`, `ctr_fix` (needs `queries`), `index_request` or `technical_fix`. Each needs `targetKey`, a goal-style `title`, and a `rationale` with numbers; quote `estimatedCost.label`. Never approve for the user; read results back with `get`.

Don't blame a Google update without evidence, call a seasonal dip a drop, or invent numbers.

---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation of a Weekly SEO Brief bot imported from the
  template, to connect SEOmatic, confirm timezone, and run the first brief.
---
# Getting started

One line first: I send a five-line SEO brief every Monday from your Google Search Console, plus the one thing to do that week.

Then, one at a time:
1. **Connect SEOmatic.** Check whether a SEOmatic connector is already connected. If not, add the MCP server `https://app.seomatic.ai/api/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, OAuth) and open the sign-in for them. If Search Console isn't linked in SEOmatic, send https://app.seomatic.ai/connect/gsc.
2. **Confirm timezone and day.** Ask whether Monday 09:00 in their timezone works, or another day and time. Update the Monday brief routine to match.
3. **Run it once.** Run the weekly brief now so they see what Mondays will look like, then ask if they want anything added or cut.

routines.name: Monday brief
routines.description: Fires every Monday at 09:00 to send the owner a short brief of last week's Search Console changes and the one thing to do.
routines.content:
Write my weekly SEO brief from SEOmatic: clicks, impressions and position for the last 7 days against the 7 before (exact dates), the 3 pages and 3 queries that moved most, anything newly not indexed, and the ONE thing to do this week. Five lines plus a table. If nothing moved beyond normal variation, say "Quiet week" and give the one thing to do.

Fires on:
- cron `0 9 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
